name: Airfrog
one_line: Coin-sized (16x28mm) wireless ARM debug co-processor on a $3 ESP32-C3-MINI-1: attaches to a target SWD header and exposes flash/RAM/peripherals over Wi-Fi instead of a wired cable.
why_notable: 60 stars, last commit 2025-09-07. Written in Rust; one of very few open wireless SWD adapters.

name: Curious Bolt
one_line: Pocket multitool combining a programmable crowbar voltage glitcher, an 8-channel logic analyzer and a differential power-analysis oscilloscope on one board; ships with an STM32F103 target and 4 challenges.
why_notable: 16 stars, last commit 2024-02-01. Vendor store page carried no price.

name: Steppenprobe
one_line: Open-hardware KiCad debug probe on an FTDI FT2232H providing simultaneous JTAG/SWD and UART/SWO over one USB-C connection, 14-pin Cortex connector, OpenOCD support.
why_notable: 44 stars, last commit 2024-07-15. DIY PCB build, no assembled price.

name: Cypherock EMFI Board
one_line: Open-hardware EMFI device converting USB power into a ~1kV pulse discharged through a hand-built EM probe, timed against a target MCU; ships with DUT boards for 7 MCU families used in crypto wallets.
why_notable: 27 stars, last commit 2024-01-06. Self-built PCB, no assembled price published.

name: ChipWhisperer Pro (CW1200)
one_line: Higher-tier ChipWhisperer capture unit. Datasheet and older docs exist but it no longer appears on NewAE's current store or ChipWhisperer product page.
why_notable: APPEARS DISCONTINUED, superseded by Husky/HuskyPlus. Worth adding with status discontinued rather than omitting, since people still own and resell these.

name: CW305 Artix FPGA Target Board
one_line: Artix-7 FPGA target board for side-channel analysis against crypto cores implemented in FPGA logic.
why_notable: APPEARS DISCONTINUED - product URL now 404s, seemingly superseded by the CW310. Same recommendation: list as discontinued.

name: GlitchCaster
one_line: Modular EMFI probe head based on the open PicoEMP design generating a roughly 250V EM pulse through a leaded or SMA probe coil; standard 40mm-fan mounting so it can be positioned by a 3D-printer or CNC stage. No built-in controller.
why_notable: Commercial EMFI tool on the same open design as the tracked ChipSHOUTER-PicoEMP, aimed at CNC-mounted repeatable glitching. Coming Soon - no funding, no price.

name: EPIC Erebus
one_line: M.2 2230 FPGA board (Lattice ECP5) for PCIe DMA research; PCILeech-compatible, supports standalone memory acquisition and patch/match without a tethered host, fully open gateware, firmware and toolchain.
why_notable: Compact PCILeech-class DMA board in M.2 form factor, distinct from the tracked Screamer PCIe Squirrel. Coming Soon - not yet funded, no price.

name: ChipJabber Unplugged
one_line: DIY-buildable voltage fault-injection kit with no programmable logic, in three build variants (through-hole, small SMD battery-powered Mini, and home-etch/PCB-mill friendly); pairs with a NOTDuino target demonstrating bypass of an EEPROM-keyed secure-boot check.
why_notable: Manual knob-tuned glitcher rather than an automated FPGA one - distinct from ChipWhisperer-Lite/Nano/Husky. Coming Soon, no price.

name: Flipper Zero Wardriving GPS enabled ESP32 Board
one_line: ESP32 with external antenna and GPS receiver as a Flipper Zero add-on, preloaded with Marauder, in a 3D-printed case; connects over serial and logs to the Flipper SD card.
why_notable: Same concept as NetNinja from a different maker at a $20 premium - a direct head-to-head comparison.

name: NetNinja Wardriving GPS Marauder
one_line: Flipper Zero expansion combining an ESP32 with a battery-backed GPS module and 2.4GHz antenna, writing geotagged Wi-Fi PCAPs to the Flipper's SD card, preloaded with Marauder.
why_notable: GPS-tagged wardriving for Flipper Zero, a capability the tracked Flipper Wi-Fi boards lack.

name: GhostBoard
one_line: Flipper Zero accessory board running the Ghost ESP firmware for WiFi 6 and BLE 5 auditing.
why_notable: Commercial Flipper-specific hardware implementation of the Ghost ESP audit suite already represented generically in the database as a bare ESP32 board.

name: Pwnagotchi Hat - UPS/GPS/AC WiFi/USB HUB/RTC all in one hat
one_line: Raspberry Pi Zero expansion board purpose-built for Pwnagotchi: dual-band AC WiFi with monitor mode/packet injection, GPS with PPS, UPS, USB hub and RTC.
why_notable: Dedicated hardware carrier for building a Pwnagotchi wardriving unit with GPS logging and battery runtime beyond the base project's typical hardware.

name: Alfa AWUS036ACHM
one_line: High-gain USB WiFi adapter with a monitor-mode/packet-injection-capable chipset, sold specifically for wireless auditing (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Standard high-sensitivity monitor-mode/injection WiFi adapter used alongside tools like the WiFi Pineapple for wardriving and deauth/capture work.

name: wardriver.uk Rev3
one_line: Dual ESP32-WROOM-32U wardriving rig with GPS, SIM800L, LCD, temp sensor and SD logging; scans Wi-Fi and Bluetooth to WiGLE-format CSV.
why_notable: 368 stars, last commit 2026-05-25. One of the longest-running open wardriving platforms, with a hosted upload service.

name: ALFA AWUS036AXM
one_line: USB Wi-Fi 6/6E + Bluetooth 5.2 adapter (MediaTek MT7921AUN), tri-band 2.4/5/6GHz, 2x detachable dipole antennas on RP-SMA; marketed here for WiFi monitor-mode capture. Sold by JCMK as an ALFA reseller, not a JCMK design.
why_notable: Commodity USB Wi-Fi adapter with real monitor-mode/capture capability (commonly paired with Pineapple/Kali-style tooling), but it is a general-purpose network adapter rather than a purpose-built security gadget.
mcu: n/a (MediaTek MT7921AUN WiFi6E/BT5.2 combo chip, no general-purpose MCU)
